answers: every peer runs the same fixed-tick simulation and only the small inputs cross the network, so there is no state to sync
lockstep sends one frame per tick, so this is your simulation's fixed step: set it to the rate your sim runs at (20 until you know)
a state hash about every 60 ticks finds a drift between peers early (a mismatch raises Desync)
a real-time round cannot wait for one player to find the pause key
the engine can listen, so players share a join code and one of them hosts: the game outlives any server
a lobby server is optional here; switch it on if you also want a public list

advice.text: Send inputs on the fast channel with the last few ticks repeated
advice.why: a reliable ordered input channel stalled one game about half its frames at 80 ms and 2% loss; redundancy on the fast channel fixed it
advice.how: no lockstep helper does this yet (its commands travel on the reliable channel); send your own input packets on the fast channel (Channel.Fast in C#, { channel: 'fast' } in JS) beside the lockstep frames

advice.text: Use an adaptive input delay (a few ticks, grown when the round trip grows)
advice.why: a fixed delay is either too laggy on a good link or too stuttery on a bad one
advice.how: no client has it yet: measure the round trip yourself and schedule each command a few ticks ahead

advice.text: Let bots take the seats of dropped players
advice.why: a lockstep game cannot wait for a player who left; a bot keeps the simulation moving
advice.how: room.on("seatDropped", s => spawnBot(s.seat)) fires once the rejoin window has passed (room.seatDropped / rejoinWindowSeconds)

questions.question: GDScript or C#? Assumed GDScript, the Godot template that exists today.
questions.add: in Godot with GDScript, or in Godot with C#

questions.question: What fixed tick rate does the simulation run at?

Is the simulation deterministic? Lockstep needs the same commands in the same order to give the same state on every peer: a fixed tick, in-state seeded random numbers, no wall clock, no unordered iteration, no floats that differ by platform (AGENTS.md rule 3).
questions.add: deterministic with a fixed tick and seeded random numbers (or: not deterministic)

runCommand: npx create-onelobby my-game --template godot-gdscript --hosting direct --mode lockstep --tick-rate 20 --set sync.hashEveryTicks=60 --max-players 4 --pause off --yes

shapes.name: Deterministic fixed-tick game
shapes.summary: party minigames, an RTS on a seeded simulation: every peer runs the same sim and only small inputs cross the network

shapes.name: Free-roam co-op with rich state
shapes.summary: survival, sandbox: the host runs the world and sends snapshots, each joiner predicts its own actions

shapes.name: Shooter or physics game, host-authoritative
shapes.summary: shooters, physics, AI: the host decides, joiners get interpolated snapshots and send inputs; anything that is not deterministic

shapes.name: Turn-based, card or board game
shapes.summary: nothing to sync between turns: the host is the truth and raw messages are enough, with no tick

shapes.name: An existing server-style game
shapes.summary: the game keeps its own server loop and OneLobby only carries the bytes, shaped like a WebSocket
